sections.label: Section A
sections.content: Clearly, when older people do heavy physical work, their age may affect their productivity. But other skills may increase with age, including many that are crucial for good management, such as an ability to handle people diplomatically, to run a meeting or to spot a problem before it blows up. Peter Hicks, who co-ordinates OECD* work on the policy implications of ageing, says that plenty of research suggests older people are paid more because they are worth more.

sections.label: Section B
sections.content: And the virtues of the young may be exaggerated. ‘The few companies that have kept on older workers find they have good judgement and their productivity is good,’ says Peter Peterson, author of a recent book on the impact of ageing. ‘Besides, their education standards are much better than those of today’s young high-school graduates.’ Companies may say that older workers are not worth training because they are reaching the end of their working lives; in fact, young people tend to switch jobs so frequently that they offer the worst returns on training.

sections.label: Section C
sections.content: The median age for employer-driven training is the late 40s and early 50s, and this training goes mainly to managers. There is no evidence that older workers are any less capable of learning new skills than younger ones. In fact, many older workers are more motivated to learn because they want to stay in the workforce longer.

sections.label: Section D
sections.content: Some companies have found that having a mix of ages in the workforce can lead to better problem-solving and innovation. Older workers can provide mentorship and guidance to younger colleagues, while younger workers can bring fresh perspectives and new ideas.

passage.title: The Impact of Urbanization on the Local Economy

sections.content: Urbanization is a global phenomenon that has significant implications for local economies. As people move from rural areas to cities in search of better opportunities, the demand for housing, infrastructure, and services increases. This shift often leads to a rise in property values and a change in the traditional business landscape. For instance, small-scale farming and local crafts may be replaced by large-scale industrial activities and modern retail outlets. While these changes can bring economic growth and new jobs, they also require the workforce to adapt to new technologies and skills.

sections.content: Conducting research in a university setting requires careful planning and a robust methodology. Students are often encouraged to start by reviewing existing literature to identify gaps in knowledge. Once a research question is formulated, the next step involves designing appropriate data collection tools, such as questionnaires or interview guides. A common concern for researchers is the sample size, as a small sample may not be representative of the broader population. Ethical approval is also a critical requirement, ensuring that the research respects the rights and privacy of participants.

sections.content: The history of human civilization is marked by a series of transformative inventions and discoveries. From the ancient use of gunpowder in China to the development of the decimal system in India, different cultures have contributed significantly to global progress. The British Industrial Revolution brought about the first steam engines, forever changing manufacturing and transport. In the Islamic world, scholars made groundbreaking advances in algebra and medicine. More recently, the digital age has been shaped by the development of internet protocols in the United States, connecting the world in unprecedented ways.
